newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BAILEY LAST OUT OF BLOCKS BUT STILL QUALIFIES EASILY.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAILEY LAST OUT OF BLOCKS BUT STILL QUALIFIES EASILY.

text.p: Donovan Bailey was last out of the blocks on Saturday as he began his defence of the world 100 metres title but recovered in time to qualify comfortably for the second round.
Running in fierce morning heat on the opening day of the sixth world championships, Bailey accelerated to take second place in his first round heat in 10.17 seconds.
Ato Boldon, who is attempting a 100-200 metres double here, clocked 10.11 seconds to win his heat while his training partner and American champion Maurice Greene also won in 10.32.
"I felt good," Boldon said. "The time is fine for the first round but you're going to have to be real fast to win the gold."
American women's champion Marion Jones, favourite for the women's 100 title, clocked 11.09 seconds in winning her heat, third fastest time of the first round.
"I could hardly sleep last night, I was so excited," Jones said. "These are my first world championships."
Briton Kelly Holmes was the first casualty of the day after competition began only 90 minutes after sunrise in order to avoid the worst of the heat.
Holmes, fastest woman in the world this year over 1,500 metres, was carried from the track grimacing with pain after pulling up with 160 metres remaining in her first round heat.

The 27-year-old Commonwealth champion, whose Olympic campaign was ruined last year because of a stress fracture in her left leg, sustained calf and Achilles tendon injuries to the same leg and will take no further part in the championships.
"I have been in the best shape of my life," she said. "I expected the gold medal."
Olympic shot put champion Randy Barnes failed to qualify for the first of Saturday's two finals when he finished only 14th in the qualifying round.
"I just don't know what happened," Barnes confessed.
The group was headed by defending champion John Godina, who finished second to Barnes in Atlanta last year.
Ukraine's Inessa Kravets, the defending women's triple jump champion, failed to start the qualifying round and Nigerian Charity Opara, third fastest woman over 400 metres this year, was also absent.
